blackrhino_c: A very young rhinoceros calf standing on four legs, only a few months old, with unmistakably infant proportions: an OVERSIZED HEAD too big for its body, SHORT STUBBY LEGS, a small rounded barrel body, a soft rounded forehead and big soft eyes. ON TOP OF ITS NOSE SITS ONE SMALL SOFT ROUNDED GREY KNOB, a low blunt bump about the size of its own eye, smooth and pebble-shaped and barely raised above the skin, sitting flat on the snout like a small river stone resting on a table - this little pebble-bump is the only thing on its nose and it is tiny, rounded and stubby, never tall, never pointed, never a spike. Below it a pointed hooked prehensile upper lip for browsing. Soft mid-grey skin, evenly and softly lit with no dark patches and no heavy shadows. Small tubular ears, a stubby tail. Its body is turned slightly away from the viewer with its head turned back toward us, so we see its face and one flank together
baskingshark: A colossal gentle plankton-straining sea creature swimming HEAD-ON STRAIGHT TOWARD THE VIEWER, seen FROM DIRECTLY IN FRONT, looking straight into its open mouth. FROM THIS ANGLE THE ANIMAL IS ONE ENORMOUS OPEN CIRCLE filling most of the picture: a VAST ROUND HOLLOW TUNNEL OPENING, dark inside like looking down a drainpipe or into a cave. ALL THE WAY AROUND THE EDGE OF THAT CIRCLE, GROWING DIRECTLY OUT OF THE RIM ITSELF AND FIXED TO IT, IS A THICK CONTINUOUS FRINGE OF FINE PALE STRAW-COLOURED HAIRS - hundreds of soft flexible bristles set into the edge exactly like the bristles of a chimney brush are set into its ring, or like the soft nap around the rim of a draught excluder. THIS SOFT HAIRY FRINGE IS THE ONLY THING ON THE RIM, it covers the whole rim completely leaving no bare part and no hard part, and every strand is thin, limp, bendy and hair-like. The fringe is part of the animal and joined to it, not a separate ring or a floating hoop. Its small dark eyes sit far out on either side of the circle and its short blunt snout rises just above it. Behind the opening a grey-brown body tapers away, pectoral fins spread wide, a tall triangular fin above
sunfishmola: A giant ocean sunfish seen in STRICT SIDE PROFILE, side-on to the viewer, one eye on the side of its head and its small round mouth at the front on the left. ITS BODY IS TALLER THAN IT IS LONG: from the top of its back down to its belly is GREATER than from its mouth back to its rear, so the flank forms a HUGE ROUND UPRIGHT PLATE, deep and round and squat like a full moon or a dinner plate stood on edge. THE BACK END OF THE ANIMAL IS THE CRITICAL PART: the disc is SHEARED CLEAN OFF, and the rear edge is A SINGLE SHORT WAVY SCALLOPED BAND OF SKIN, a low ruffle of small rounded bumps LYING FLAT AND FLUSH AGAINST THE CUT LIKE THE CRIMPED EDGE OF A PIE CRUST or the frilled hem of a lettuce leaf, hugging the body tightly and standing out from it no further than the animal's own eye is wide. THAT CRIMPED HEM IS THE ENTIRE BACK END and it is the last thing on the animal - beyond it there is only empty water. From the TOP of the circle ONE ENORMOUS POINTED FIN rises straight UP and from the BOTTOM one identical fin points straight DOWN, and those two are the only large fins. A tiny round mouth, one large round eye, small pectoral fins, rough mottled silver-grey hide
